title: Amos White, and a Creole jazz band job that ended in a brawl
summary: Vincent talks about Amos White, then tells of his Creole jazz band playing a rough job where drunken patrons turned on them, and the band left with about $35 each.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: I didn't know him. You never know that? He's in California.

He wasn't from here. I didn't forget where he was. But he'd come down there and stay at Goodwire. He was a learning type of printing. And Lewis used to come around us all the time. He was a professor. You know, he was a musician. And we played with him. I had the Marlene Creole jazz band. That's right there. And the bass player was the darkest one in the band. And we played on. You know what I told you that time? The old Apsom. It was named, let me see what was his name. I didn't call his name before. Hawkins. Hawkins, yeah. Hawkins Sluth. And the first is he used to come and get it. You know, play. And he used to give his mother by the hand for it. Tell me to get drunk the bar back if he stayed there. The bar had a hole back in there. And they come and look and say, what kind of band is this? He said, you're white, you're Mexican, you're men. He said, this is this. Hi, you're the Creole Negro band. And we told him, yeah. And then after that, when they started, the captain, Captain John, he came there and he got pulled out of the peace. And so him, he said, man, we better get out there now. I said, they're getting drunk to come back here and borrow everything. And we started packing up on the slides, still playing, reading one by one. And when we seen there was so interesting talking, they get the whole band left, pull away the drink out of the drums. He was the last one that they ran up. So I went back and grabbed his, you know, his slides there. And we left. We come out with about $35 a piece, you know. If they charge him to make a price for him, they pay you that price. But if you don't charge him, they give you a plan of money. If you don't have them guys come in there, get drunk and borrow his back from him, you know.
